orig_text:
6.  Let PATTERN be a "URL pattern struct" created by running the
    steps to "create a URL pattern" by setting input=MATCH and
    baseURL=URL (see Section 1.4 of [URLPATTERN]).
correct_text:
6.  Let PATTERN be a "URL pattern struct" created by running the
    steps to "create a URL pattern" by setting input=MATCH and
    baseURL=BASEURL (see Section 1.4 of [URLPATTERN]).
notes:
Step 2 defines BASEURL as the dictionary request URL, while step 3
defines URL as the outbound request URL. Step 6 uses the latter as
the base for constructing the dictionary's match pattern. Relative
patterns therefore acquire a different meaning depending on the
outbound request.

For example, a dictionary at https://example.com/assets/dict.bin
with match="*" has pathname pattern /assets/* when constructed as
specified in Section 2.1.1. For an outbound request to
https://example.com/private/account, Section 2.2.2 instead constructs
/private/* and returns a match. Using BASEURL retains /assets/* and
does not match. Conversely, match="child/*" can fail to match the
intended /assets/child/page because the published operand constructs
/assets/child/child/*.

The correction restores the dictionary request URL as the base.
The outbound request URL remains the matching input in step 7.
The same-origin and destination checks remain unchanged. The
baseURL=URL expression in Section 2.1.1 is correct and is not changed:
URL there denotes the dictionary request URL.

This reports an algorithm error, not an observed deployed failure.
